title: recomplauncher.json
description: How RecompLauncher sets up, starts and configures a recomp. See docs/DEVELOPERS.md.

inputs.description: Named game/disc/DLC inputs, explicit shared-key requirements, and NVIDIA's DLSS file (nvidia.dlss). See SETUP-INPUTS.md. No multidisc hashing, BIOS, firmware or font support.

role.description: runtime: a file the launcher fetches itself (nvidia.dlss); the player picks nothing.

shared.description: Shared across games. nvidia.dlss: NVIDIA's nvngx_dlss.dll, downloaded from NVIDIA by the launcher on NVIDIA RTX PCs. Coming soon to RecompLauncher; older launchers show an error for it, so add it once the version that has it is out.

destination.description: Optional installation-relative file path. No folders, absolute paths, parent components or placeholders.

requires.description: IDs of required shared-key inputs in this manifest, activated only for this selected format.

name.description: Your recomp's name, as players see it. The launcher shows it for a build added from a folder (Developer tools); a listed recomp uses its name on recomplauncher.com.

repo.description: Your GitHub repo, owner/name. Only needed for profiles built into the launcher.

game.description: The player's own copy of the game.

label.description: What to ask for. Name the region or serial if only one works.

check.description: How to tell it's the right game.

file.description: A file in the game's folder, like default.xex.

xdvdfs.description: A file on an Xbox 360 disc image.

iso9660.description: A file in the top folder of a PS2 (or any ISO 9660) disc image.

nup_build_id.description: The build ID of a Nintendo Switch or Switch 2 .nup package (hex, 8 to 64 digits; a prefix such as the first 8 is fine), read from the exefs/main of its newest title. A folder with exefs/main is checked the same way. Judged by the file's content, never its name. Needs no keys.

ids.description: The disc or cartridge IDs it reads, as on the copy: a GameCube or Wii disc's (GZ2E01, or GZ2 for every region), an N64 cartridge's game code, a PlayStation disc's serial. Another game's copy is refused, and the player's copies are recognised by it.

dumps.description: Known good dumps (from Redump), for the verified badge.

update.description: A second thing the game needs beside the player's copy, picked on its own (a title update, or a PS4 update folder kept apart from the game). The launcher puts it in the game's folder and keeps it across updates.

into.description: The folder inside your release it goes in, like game/Content or update.

label.description: What to ask for, like 'Your title update (TU 1.03)'.

accepts.description: Whether the player picks a file, a folder, or either.

optional.description: The game plays without it; the player can skip it.

name.description: The name it must have there (it's put in under this name).

sha256.description: The one known file: checked when it's picked.

env.description: Environment variables for your game, like SDL hints. Paths such as {install} fill in. RECOMPLAUNCHER_ names and system ones like PATH are left out.

prepare.description: Your own setup step, run without a window after the copy is checked.

game_path.description: The key that holds the path to the player's copy.

new.description: Set when the file is created.

folders.description: Named places. 'saves' and 'logs' are used by the launcher itself.

exit_codes.description: Exit code (as a string) to the message shown to the player. "ok" instead of a message: the game closes with that code when it's quit normally, so it isn't shown as a crash.

in.description: A config id, or 'args' for the command line.

defaults.description: The game's own values for keys the file doesn't have yet.

when.description: Greyed out unless these keys have these values.

group.description: A heading it's shown under, like "Controls". Settings keep their order; a heading shows where the group changes.

advanced.description: Hidden until the player presses Show Advanced Options. Its value stays, and it's still written.

slider.description: A number on a slider instead of choices. The value is read from "key" like "set" keys (Section/Key), and written with "format". A value off the step (set in the game's own menu) is shown as it is and left alone until the player moves the slider.

key.description: The key it sets in the settings file (Section/Key for INI sections and TOML tables). Not needed with "in": "args".

step.description: How far one move goes. A hundredth of the range when it isn't said.

format.description: How the number is written, printf style: "%.2f", "%d", "%g".

args.description: With "in": "args": the arguments, with {value} for the number. The same as the setting's own "args".
For a slider with "in": "args": its arguments, with {value} for the number, like ["--sens", "{value}"]. Passed only once the player has moved it.

bindings.description: Key bindings instead of choices: the game's actions, each with the keys it's on in the settings file. The game page shows each action with its keys as chips; the player presses a chip and then the new key, mouse button or wheel. Only actions the player changes are written.

separator.description: Joins several keys on one action, in the order the player set them. Default "|".

max.description: Keys one action can have. Default 2.

key.description: Where it's written, with the same rules as "set": Section/Key for INI or TOML, nested/keys for JSON.

pad.description: It takes a controller button too.

names.description: The launcher's name for a key or button, to the name your file uses for it, like {"Return": "Enter"}. Without one, a name the file already uses for that key is kept.

groups.description: Groups used in settings' "group". A group marked advanced is hidden as a whole until the player shows advanced options.

id.description: The name the settings use in "group".

saves.description: Where the game keeps its saves: folders, files, or files matching a * pattern. Backups and cloud saves copy these.

looks.description: Looks (ReShade filters) for this game. Leave it out and they work with what the launcher works out itself.

allowed.description: false if your recomp has its own filters, or ReShade doesn't work with it.

reason.description: Shown to the player when looks are off.

graphics.description: The graphics API your recomp draws with.

graphics_key.description: A settings key that holds the graphics API the player picked, in the config named by 'in'.

lines.description: Lines for the CRT looks, when the console's usual number is wrong for your game.

mods.description: Where players get mods for your game. Leave it out if the launcher already knows (Zelda 64: Recompiled, Banjo: Recompiled, Unleashed Recompiled, Marathon Recompiled and the Ship of Harkinian family).

thunderstore.description: Your Thunderstore community, as in thunderstore.io/c/<community>. Needs 'data'.

data.description: Your data folder's name (in AppData\Local on Windows, ~/.config on Linux). Mods go in its mods folder, or in the game's own mods folder when portable.txt is there.

gamebanana.description: Your game's id on GameBanana, as in gamebanana.com/games/<id>. Needs 'loader'.

loader.description: How your game reads mods: nrm (.nrm files in the data folder's mods folder, needs 'data'), otr (.otr and .o2r files in a mods folder next to the executable) or hmm (Hedge Mod Manager mods with a mod.ini, needs 'user').

user.description: For hmm: your folder in AppData\Roaming that holds cpkredir.ini.

clear.description: A folder name and subfolder, like saves/cache.

requires.description: The launcher features this profile uses. Parts needing a feature the player's launcher doesn't have are left out (no Easy Setup, no settings tab for it); the game still installs and plays.

min.description: The oldest launcher version this profile's Easy Setup, settings and installer parts work with, like "0.90.0-beta.27". Older launchers leave those parts out.

programs.description: Paths inside your release, tried in order.

values.description: Key to value, written exactly as given (TOML strings keep their quotes).

if.description: Used only when this path exists.

launcherFeature.description: A launcher feature a profile can say it uses ("requires"). A launcher that doesn't have one leaves out the parts that need it, and the game installs and plays the normal way. RecompLauncher 0.90 Beta 27 supports these.
